C01.text: The first wave of the Grande Armee crossed the Neman on 24 June 1812: more than 450,000 men and over 150,000 horses.

C02.text: About 100,000 French troops entered Moscow on 14 September 1812.

C04.text: Napoleon trained as an artillery officer; he preferred the offensive and aimed to destroy the enemy's army in battle.

C05.text: The Gribeauval 12-pounder: effective range about 900 m with round shot and 600 m with canister; a crew of 15.

C06.text: The Charleville musket was effective to about 100 yards (90 m), two or three shots a minute.

C07.text: Infantry squares held their volley until cavalry was very close; a steady square was rarely broken by cavalry alone, artillery was its main danger.

C08.text: Each Mongol soldier kept three or four horses and changed mounts on the march.

C09.text: Mongol composite bows: aimed shots at about 150-175 m, ballistic shots up to about 400 m; a quiver of 60 arrows.

C10.text: Kalka River, 31 May 1223: the Rus princes had killed the Mongol envoys; Jebe and Subutai drew them on in a feigned retreat of about nine days and destroyed them; captured princes were crushed under a victory platform.

C11.text: Genghis Khan promoted by merit and loyalty, kept the enemy archer Jebe who had shot his horse and admitted it, and recruited skilled men from defeated enemies.

C12.text: Moscow was abandoned by Kutuzov's army and burned (Governor Rostopchin); Alexander I refused to negotiate; the French left on 19 October after about five weeks.

C13.text: Murat was the best cavalry commander of the Grande Armee and showed a total lack of concern for the well-being of his horses.

C14.text: The Mameluke company of the Imperial Guard served in Russia in 1812 (109 riders on 1 July); its men came from Crimea, Georgia, Circassia, Syria, Egypt and elsewhere.

C15.text: Crimean Tatar and Cuman (the Kipchak of the 13th-century steppe) are both Kipchak Turkic languages.

C16.text: The army's supply rested on heavy wagons unfit for Russian tracks; foraging along the road fed the rest ('the Army must live by the sword', Colonel Pion).

C19.text: Genghis Khan stopped his Central Asian campaign in 1221 and was back in Mongolia by 1225; in 1223 he was not on the western steppe.

C20.text: A tumen was a Mongol unit of 10,000 men.

CH1.text: The channel's episodes: 100 geniuses in the Stone Age (on the channel); 100 people dropped into the Ice Age (coming next).

I01.text: The fog that drops the army from 1812 into the steppe of 1223, and back.

I02.text: Genghis Khan himself on the western steppe in 1223 with about two tumens.

I03.text: The skirmish, the valley battle, the burning of the wagons and their numbers.

I04.text: The parley and the two guns left to the khan.
